reason: The fast rocky projectiles are the obvious remaining stones for the world to encounter.

choice.combine: The rocky world with a small moon

expectation: The projectiles will strike the rocky world as it continues its journey with its moon.

effect: The world needed to be combined with its host star, which automatically completed its encounter with the remaining stones.
reaction: I was surprised the star, rather than the projectiles, was the required partner.
reason: The exposed inner disk is the natural place to follow the exposed gas and dust as they escape.

choice.combine: Exposed gas carrying small dust grains

expectation: The exposed disk material will disperse outward into the galaxy.

effect: The exposed disk returned gas and dust to the nursery early in the system's history, completing the remaining goal.
reaction: I liked the contrast between early disk loss and the much longer history of rocky collisions.

mostWorthwhile.text: Following the escaping disk material was most worthwhile: it connected the young planetary system back to its galactic surroundings and clarified the different timescales involved.

leastWorthwhile.text: The attempted collision with the projectiles was the least clear passage: the world instead needed the host star as its partner, although the automatic combination kept play moving.

surprise.text: I expected the rocky world to combine directly with the projectiles, so the host star being the required partner surprised me.

arbitrary.text: Using the host star rather than the visible projectiles for the stones encounter felt somewhat arbitrary, even though the result explained the wider view.

continue.text: I would choose to continue: the connection between disk material escaping early and later planetary collisions made me curious about what happens next.
